scams.name: London Coach-Tour 'Stonehenge + Bath + Windsor' Combo Package Fraud
scams.description: The single most-booked UK coach-tour product for older US/Canadian travelers is the London-to-Stonehenge-to-Bath-to-Windsor day-trip, sold via Viator, GetYourGuide, TripAdvisor Experiences, Golden Tours, and Evan Evans at £99–£145 per person. For tourists with 4-7 days in London, it's pitched as 'three iconic sites in one day.' The UK-resident community consensus is blunt. r/uktravel 'Is a Windsor/Stonehenge/Bath day trip from London worth it?' (comments/1d6kmoj, late 2024) top comment: 'No, those package tours are kind of a scam — you'll spend most of [the day on a coach].' r/uktravel 'What is the most common mistake tourists make in the UK?' (comments/1aupp30, 2024) flags the coach-tour over-packing pattern. r/uktravel 'Stonehenge and Windsor Castle Tour' (comments/1m3kpd8, mid-2025) documents new 2025 variants selling the same pattern. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) the 8-10 hour coach day breaks down to approximately 45-60 min AT Stonehenge (just the audio-guide loop, no Inner Circle access), 90-120 min in Bath (rushed lunch + Roman Baths exterior + no Pump Room tea), 30-45 min at Windsor (exterior only — no State Apartments), and 5-6 hours of coach transit; (2) the 'shopping stop' pattern — tours include a designated Cotswolds village or motorway-service shopping stop where guides receive commission; (3) the Stonehenge ticket included in these tours is the Stone Circle Access 'exterior only' ticket at £23 adult value, NOT the Inner Circle Early Access / Evening Access (£80-£110, separate booking required); (4) the Bath itinerary gives NO time for Thermae Bath Spa, Jane Austen Centre, or a sit-down meal; (5) the Windsor stop is often 'external only' — meaning you see the castle from the Long Walk but don't enter the State Apartments (which require Windsor Castle admission at £33.50 separate); (6) refund windows are highly restrictive — tour operators sell 'non-refundable' bookings when TripAdvisor Experiences and Viator standard policy is 24-hour cancellation; (7) older travelers on tight trip budgets lose opportunity cost — 3 rushed sites in 1 day vs 1 properly-planned day per destination; (8) the coach-tour target demographic is specifically older North American travelers unused to UK train networks — the whole product is calibrated for this group. For older travelers with Stonehenge, Bath, or Windsor on their London day-trip shortlist: (1) pick ONE destination per day — don't try to combine three in one day; (2) for Stonehenge specifically: take the direct train from London Waterloo to Salisbury (90 min, £25-£45 off-peak), then the Stonehenge Tour Bus (£17 round-trip from Salisbury Station, 20-30 min journey, admission extra at £23 direct at english-heritage.org.uk) — total £65-£85 per person, 6 hours door-to-door, 2+ hours AT Stonehenge; (3) for Bath, direct train from London Paddington (90 min, £25-£65 off-peak); (4) for Windsor, direct train from London Waterloo (55 min, £11-£15); (5) if you MUST do a combo day-tour, use Rabbie's Tours (Edinburgh-based, higher-quality coach operators, £95-£110) or Evan Evans 'Stonehenge Only' trip — confirm your tour lists Stone Circle Inner Access (£80+) if you want to walk among the stones, otherwise you're just paying for exterior viewing; (6) refuse any 'shopping stop' over 20 min; (7) for coach-tour refunds, TripAdvisor Experiences / Viator standard policy is 24-hour cancellation — insist on this, decline 'non-refundable' bookings; (8) for older travelers with mobility concerns, a dedicated Stonehenge day with the Tour Bus is far less physically taxing than the 3-city 10-hour coach marathon.
scams.avoidance: Pick ONE destination per day — Stonehenge via Salisbury train (90 min, £25-£45) + Tour Bus (£17) For Inner Circle Access: book at english-heritage.org.uk 2-3 months ahead (£80-£110) If you must book a combo tour, use Rabbie's Tours or Evan Evans 'Stonehenge Only' — not 3-city combos Refuse any 'shopping stop' over 20 min — insist on skipping or wait in the coach Confirm 24-hr refund window before booking — refuse 'non-refundable' deals via Viator/GetYourGuide
scams.location: London Victoria Coach Station, London Paddington, tour-operator pickup zones — targeting visitors booking Stonehenge combo day-trips

scams.name: Stone Circle Inner Access Third-Party Reseller Markup
scams.description: The Stone Circle Inner Access experience — English Heritage's ticketed early-morning or evening session that lets 30 people walk AMONG the standing stones (vs the normal audio-guide loop that stops at 10m distance) — is the premier Stonehenge experience. Official pricing is £80-£110 per person direct at english-heritage.org.uk, booked 2-3 months ahead for summer. The exclusivity and demand create a third-party reseller market that marks up the same access 2-3x. r/uktravel 'Stonehenge Stone Circle Access' (comments/1ajl0qs, early 2025) documents the community's understanding of the official product. r/Stonehenge 'Stone Circle Access pricing' (comments/1lmhe5t, mid-2025) reinforces the £80-£110 direct price. r/uktravel 'Stonehenge private tour operators' (comments/1nvvfbw, late 2025) names the third-party pattern specifically — Premium Tours and similar operators sell 'Stonehenge VIP access' at £180-£250 per person for what's £80-£110 direct, plus they charge for their own transport bundling. r/travel 'Viator/GetYourGuide tickets three times more expensive' (comments/njgudt) documents the cross-attraction reseller inflation pattern. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) Stone Circle Access tickets release in waves — about 12 months, 6 months, and then monthly ahead of each season; summer weekends fill within hours of release; (2) third-party resellers buy up tickets in bulk using multiple accounts, then resell at 2-3x with bundled transport; (3) the bundled 'luxury private tour from London' is priced at £279-£450 per person but the actual Stone Circle Access ticket is the same £80-£110 value — you're paying £200-£350 for the car + driver + 'private guide' who is often a freelance unlicensed operator; (4) some resellers advertise 'guaranteed Stone Circle Access' for specific dates when tickets are already sold out — these deliver either refused entry at the site or a wait list; (5) the Stonehenge Visitor Centre staff confirm only official English Heritage QR codes and identity — resellers' 'voucher' tickets require name-match on the booking; (6) older travelers often pre-book from North America months ahead, then arrive to find their third-party 'voucher' doesn't work at the gate; (7) the legitimate alternative for small-group Inner Access: English Heritage members get priority booking access AND a 15% discount — membership is £78/year (£134 joint) and pays for itself if you visit 3+ English Heritage sites during a UK trip. For older travelers wanting Stone Circle Inner Access: (1) book DIRECTLY at english-heritage.org.uk — no reseller, no aggregator, no 'luxury tour company'; (2) monitor the English Heritage release calendar — tickets for April-September typically release in December-January, September-March tickets in July-August; (3) summer weekend slots sell out within hours — have the website open at release time and book immediately; (4) consider becoming an English Heritage Member (£78/year individual, £134 joint) for priority-release access and 15% discounts across 400+ UK historic sites — excellent value if you're planning UK trips for 2+ years; (5) for transport, book the direct train London Waterloo to Salisbury (90 min, £25-£45 off-peak) + Stonehenge Tour Bus (£17 round-trip, 20-30 min journey) — total £65-£85 per person for transport; (6) refuse ALL 'private luxury Stonehenge tour' offers at £279-£450 — these are transport bundles around the £80-£110 you could book directly; (7) for older travelers who want a private driver, Crown Coaches (licensed) offers Salisbury-based private driver at £180-£280 per half-day that will pick you up and return you with flexibility — still better value than aggregator 'VIP tours'; (8) at the Visitor Centre, bring the original English Heritage QR code AND ID matching the booking name — resellers' 'vouchers' are often refused entry; (9) if a reseller site fails to deliver access, dispute via UK Section 75 Consumer Credit Act (credit cards, min £100) or Visa/MC chargeback.
scams.avoidance: Book DIRECTLY at english-heritage.org.uk — no reseller, no aggregator, no 'luxury tour' Consider English Heritage Membership (£78/year) for priority-release access + 15% discounts Monitor the release calendar — summer slots release Dec-Jan, winter slots release Jul-Aug For transport: London Waterloo → Salisbury train (£25-45) + Stonehenge Tour Bus (£17) = £65-85 total Refuse 'private luxury Stonehenge tour' at £279-£450 — you're paying £200+ markup on £80-110 access
scams.location: Stonehenge Visitor Centre (Amesbury, Wiltshire), third-party tour aggregator websites — targeting Stone Circle Early Access / Evening Access tickets

scams.name: Stonehenge Tour Bus From Salisbury — Third-Party Ticket Reseller
scams.description: The Stonehenge Tour Bus (operated by Salisbury Reds, the local Go South Coast subsidiary) is the standard public-transport way to reach Stonehenge from Salisbury railway station. Official fare is £17 round-trip adult (includes Stonehenge admission at Visitor Centre option OR stand-alone bus ticket at £17) direct at thestonehengetour.info, running every 30 min from Salisbury Station via Salisbury Cathedral and Old Sarum to Stonehenge. Over 2024-2025, r/salisburyuk and r/Stonehenge have documented a rising pattern of third-party 'Salisbury-Stonehenge transport' bookings that resell the same bus at 2x markup with fake 'priority boarding' pitches. r/salisburyuk 'Stonehenge Tour Bus from Salisbury' (comments/1so0fsq, late 2025) documents the current pricing confusion. r/Stonehenge 'Salisbury Tour Bus route' (comments/1so16pn, late 2025) covers the official route and pricing. r/uktravel 'From Salisbury to Stonehenge transport' (comments/1eiz3dn, early 2025) names the legitimate operator. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) third-party reseller sites (stonehenge-tour.com, salisbury-stonehenge-bus.co.uk and SEO variants) display the £17 price prominently then add £3-£6 'booking fee' + £2-£4 'priority boarding' at checkout, bringing final price to £24-£30; (2) the 'priority boarding' premium doesn't exist — Stonehenge Tour Bus seats on a first-come basis; (3) some resellers sell 'combo tickets' (Salisbury Tour Bus + Stonehenge admission) at £55-£65 when the legitimate combo is £36 (£17 bus + £23 admission, often discounted to £35 combined by Salisbury Reds); (4) 'taxi from Salisbury Station to Stonehenge' offered by unlicensed operators at £35-£50 one-way (vs £17 round-trip on the Tour Bus) — the unlicensed drivers at Salisbury Station are a documented pattern per r/uktravel 'Salisbury Station taxi' (comments/1hfkjbg, late 2024) which names 'allthesevens' as the only licensed Salisbury operator and warns Uber doesn't operate in Salisbury; (5) at Salisbury Railway Station, tour-bus touts intercept visitors with 'skip-the-queue Stonehenge' pitches at £25-£30 — the legitimate queue for the Tour Bus is 5-10 min and orderly; (6) older travelers pre-booking from North America often can't tell which site is the official Salisbury Reds vs a reseller; (7) Salisbury Reds runs a '3-in-1 combo' (Tour Bus + Cathedral + Old Sarum) at £22-£27 legitimate pricing — this is worth verifying at the Salisbury Reds office or Salisbury Station ticket desk rather than via third-party sites. For older travelers traveling Salisbury-Stonehenge: (1) book Stonehenge Tour Bus ONLY at thestonehengetour.info or buy walk-up at Salisbury Station (there's a dedicated Tour Bus ticket desk in the station concourse); (2) the legitimate combo Tour Bus + Stonehenge admission is £35-£38 (often on sale together at the Visitor Centre) — if a reseller quotes £55+ they're marking up; (3) refuse ALL 'priority boarding' premium offers — the Tour Bus doesn't sell this; (4) for Salisbury Station taxis, use Allthesevens (+44-1722-333-777, the licensed Salisbury operator per r/uktravel comments/1hfkjbg, 2024) — Uber does NOT operate in Salisbury; (5) decline 'Stonehenge + Salisbury Cathedral + Old Sarum' combo tickets over £30 per person — Salisbury Reds' own 3-in-1 is £22-£27; (6) for older travelers with mobility concerns, the Tour Bus has wheelchair access; request at ticket booking; (7) if a third-party reseller fails to deliver a valid Tour Bus ticket, dispute via UK Section 75 Consumer Credit Act (credit cards, min £100); (8) for transport London-Salisbury, book the direct train at gwr.com (London Waterloo to Salisbury, 90 min, £25-£45 off-peak) — UK Senior Railcard (£30/year, age 60+) drops fares 34%.
scams.avoidance: Book Tour Bus at thestonehengetour.info or walk-up at Salisbury Station ticket desk — £17 round-trip Legitimate combo Tour Bus + Stonehenge admission is £35-£38 — refuse reseller quotes above For Salisbury Station taxi, use Allthesevens (+44-1722-333-777, licensed) — NO Uber in Salisbury Refuse 'priority boarding' premium offers — Tour Bus seats on first-come basis For London-Salisbury train, book at gwr.com (90 min, £25-45 off-peak, UK Senior Railcard saves 34%)
scams.location: Salisbury Railway Station pickup zone, Salisbury Cathedral Close stop, Stonehenge Visitor Centre return stop — targeting the £17 official Stonehenge Tour Bus route

scams.name: Summer & Winter Solstice Over-Pricing & 'Free Entry' Confusion
scams.description: English Heritage runs two major Solstice events per year at Stonehenge — the Summer Solstice (around 21 June) and Winter Solstice (around 21 December) — during which the stones are open for 'Managed Open Access' allowing thousands of visitors (~8,000 at Summer Solstice) to walk among the stones at sunrise. These events are FREE to attend — the only legitimate cost is £15-£25 for parking (pre-booked via the National Trust car park) and transport to Amesbury. The free-entry nature creates confusion that third-party operators exploit by selling 'Solstice Experience' packages at £89-£249 per person. r/salisburyuk 'Stonehenge Summer Solstice 2025' (comments/1jyvlyk, mid-2025) documents the free-entry nature and parking logistics. r/uktravel 'Stonehenge Solstice confusion' (comments/1hrbp61, late 2024) documents the reseller overpricing pattern. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) Solstice attendance is FREE but parking must be pre-booked via english-heritage.org.uk (£15-£25) — this is the ONLY legitimate charge; (2) third-party operators sell 'Solstice Experience' tickets at £89-£249 claiming 'exclusive access' that doesn't exist (all Solstice access is free, first-come); (3) some tour operators bundle 'Solstice transport from London' at £149-£299 per person with the free-admission Solstice access presented as 'included' — the £150-£250 markup is for the coach transport; (4) unofficial 'Solstice camping' sites near Amesbury charge £75-£149 per night for tent pitches that are normally free or £10-£20 at local campsites; (5) Solstice Weekend is NOT the same as Solstice Day — resellers sometimes sell 'Solstice Weekend Access' for a 3-day window that has no basis in actual event logistics; (6) Winter Solstice (21 December) has a smaller crowd (typically 1,000-2,000 attendees) and easier parking but same £15-£25 parking fee structure; (7) older travelers are particularly vulnerable because Summer Solstice starts at sunrise (around 4:45 AM) and requires overnight presence — scammers exploit this by selling 'Solstice hotel + access' packages at £299-£499 that bundle any Salisbury hotel at 2-3x markup; (8) English Heritage partners with Stonehenge Alliance for sacred druid/pagan ceremony access — these are free-access events within the main Solstice timeframe. For older travelers interested in Summer or Winter Solstice at Stonehenge: (1) attendance is FREE — do not pay for 'access' or 'Solstice ticket' from any reseller; (2) book parking ONLY at english-heritage.org.uk (£15-£25) 4-6 weeks ahead of the event; (3) for Summer Solstice, the stones open at sunset before Solstice Day (20 June) through sunrise on 21 June — plan for overnight; (4) shuttle buses run from various Amesbury and Salisbury points to the Visitor Centre during the event — check the English Heritage site for the current year's transport; (5) for Salisbury hotels during Solstice, book directly (The Red Lion, Mercure White Hart, Cathedral Hotel) 3-6 months ahead — rates genuinely rise but not to the £299-£499 'Solstice package' levels resellers charge; (6) for Winter Solstice (21 December), a much quieter and less crowded experience — book parking 2-3 weeks ahead; (7) if you just want to SEE sunrise at the stones without the crowds, Stone Circle Inner Access (£80-£110, different English Heritage product) gives 30-person private access year-round; (8) refuse ALL 'Solstice VIP' or 'Druid Ceremony Access' tours that claim restrictions — these ceremonies are open to anyone attending the free Solstice event; (9) for older travelers uncomfortable with the dawn-start crowds, Winter Solstice (noon arrival, sunset at 4 PM) is more manageable than Summer Solstice.
scams.avoidance: Solstice attendance is FREE — do not pay for 'access' or 'Solstice ticket' from any reseller Book parking ONLY at english-heritage.org.uk (£15-£25) 4-6 weeks ahead of the event For Salisbury hotels, book directly (The Red Lion, Mercure White Hart, Cathedral Hotel) 3-6 months ahead For year-round dawn-access experience, book Stone Circle Inner Access at £80-£110 (30-person private) Winter Solstice (21 Dec) is a much quieter alternative — Summer (21 June) requires 3 AM arrival
scams.location: Stonehenge Visitor Centre (Amesbury) — Summer Solstice (21 June) and Winter Solstice (21 December) Managed Open Access events

scams.name: Salisbury Station Taxi & Unlicensed Private-Hire Overcharges
scams.description: Salisbury is a small UK market town with a tourist-heavy station serving London-Stonehenge day-trippers (LSW from London Waterloo, 90 min). The taxi/private-hire situation is unusual: Uber does NOT operate in Salisbury, and only one licensed operator (Allthesevens Taxis) handles the bulk of legitimate work. This creates fertile ground for unlicensed private-hire drivers who exploit tourist unfamiliarity. r/uktravel 'Salisbury Station taxi' (comments/1hfkjbg, late 2024) names the situation explicitly: 'allthesevens' is the only legit operator, no Uber. r/salisburyuk 'Salisbury transport options' (comments/1kxz49w, mid-2025) reinforces the Uber-absent pattern. r/LondonTravel 'From Salisbury to Stonehenge' (comments/1qw6jun, late 2025) documents current taxi-fare expectations. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) exit Salisbury Railway Station concourse and licensed Hackney Carriages line up on South Western Road — these are metered and safe; (2) unlicensed private-hire drivers intercept visitors INSIDE the station concourse with 'taxi to Stonehenge?' pitches — these are unregulated, no meter, and quote £35-£60 one-way for what should be £17 round-trip on the Tour Bus; (3) the 'Stonehenge taxi package' variant offers a 2-hour round-trip at £80-£120 per person — but the driver often drops visitors 'at the edge' of the Stonehenge site (not the Visitor Centre) and returns them to Salisbury from a different pickup point; (4) Uber is confirmed NOT available in Salisbury (per r/uktravel comments/1hfkjbg) — any 'Uber' offered is therefore a scam; (5) Bolt and FreeNow similarly don't operate — the only legitimate ride-hail is taxi dispatch via Allthesevens Taxis (+44-1722-333-777); (6) for Salisbury Station to Salisbury Cathedral (10 minutes walk or 3-minute taxi), legitimate metered fare is £6-£10; for Salisbury Station to Stonehenge Visitor Centre (20 min drive), legitimate one-way taxi is £30-£45 metered — refuse quotes above £50; (7) older travelers with mobility concerns are specifically targeted because walking from Salisbury Station to the Cathedral (10 min) or the Tour Bus pickup is perceived as difficult; (8) the Tour Bus (£17 round-trip with admission add-on, stops at Salisbury Station, Salisbury Cathedral, Old Sarum, and Stonehenge Visitor Centre) is the community-recommended alternative for any older traveler. For older travelers arriving at Salisbury Railway Station: (1) exit the station, walk to the licensed Hackney Carriage rank on South Western Road — these are metered and safe; (2) refuse EVERY 'taxi to Stonehenge?' offer from anyone inside the station concourse — these are unlicensed, unregulated, and quote 2-3x legitimate fares; (3) for pre-booked taxi to Stonehenge or city centre, call Allthesevens Taxis (+44-1722-333-777) — the only licensed Salisbury operator per r/uktravel community; (4) for the Stonehenge trip, STRONGLY consider the Stonehenge Tour Bus (£17 round-trip from Salisbury Station, every 30 min) instead of a taxi — it's the cheapest, most scam-proof, and community-recommended option; (5) metered Salisbury Station to Salisbury Cathedral is £6-£10; Salisbury Station to Stonehenge is £30-£45 one-way — refuse quotes above; (6) Uber, Bolt, and FreeNow do NOT operate in Salisbury — any 'Uber' pitch is a scam; (7) Salisbury is small — Salisbury Cathedral is 10 minutes walk from the Station on flat paths and is community-recommended for older travelers who are comfortable walking; (8) report unlicensed taxi-touts at Salisbury Station to Wiltshire Police non-emergency 101 and Wiltshire Council Licensing at +44-1225-713-000.
scams.avoidance: Exit Salisbury Station, walk to licensed Hackney Carriage rank on South Western Road — metered and safe For pre-booked taxi, call Allthesevens Taxis (+44-1722-333-777, the only licensed Salisbury operator) For Stonehenge, use the Tour Bus (£17 round-trip from Salisbury Station, every 30 min) — cheapest and safest Salisbury Cathedral is 10 min walk from Station on flat paths — walk if mobility permits NO Uber/Bolt/FreeNow in Salisbury — any such pitch is a scam
scams.location: Salisbury Railway Station exit, Salisbury city centre taxi ranks — targeting arriving Stonehenge-bound tourists

scams.name: Private Stonehenge Tour Operator Unlicensed Guides & Viator Markup
scams.description: The 'private luxury Stonehenge tour' market has exploded on Viator, GetYourGuide, TripAdvisor Experiences, and direct operator websites since 2023, selling bespoke 'chauffeur + guide' Stonehenge experiences at £279-£450 per person. r/travel 'Viator/GetYourGuide tickets three times more expensive' (comments/njgudt) is the canonical cross-attraction reseller documentation. r/uktravel 'Stonehenge private tour operators' (comments/1nvvfbw, late 2025) names the specific Stonehenge-market operators — Premium Tours London is the largest brand. r/EuropeTravelHacks 'How to book Stonehenge cheap' (comments/1rekr8f) documents the direct-book vs private-tour differential: £80-£110 direct Inner Access vs £279-£450 'private tour' for the same access. The specific mechanics affecting older travelers: (1) the 'private luxury' framing targets older US/Canadian travelers who associate 'private guide + driver' with higher-quality experience vs group coach tour; (2) pricing breakdown — the actual Stonehenge admission cost £23 general or £80-£110 Inner Circle Access; the 'guide' is typically a freelance unlicensed operator earning £80-£150 per day; the 'driver' is a commercial taxi or black-cab driver earning £150-£250 per day; the aggregator platform takes 20-30% commission; (3) 'Inner Circle Access + Private Guide + Round-Trip from London' bundles at £279-£450 per person mean the actual cost stack is £110 (Inner Circle) + £150-£200 (transport) + £100-£150 (guide) + platform commission — your markup is typically £50-£100 per person; (4) UNLICENSED guides are the specific risk — UK Blue Badge Guides (the only fully licensed national tour guide qualification) are quality-verified and do sometimes work on Stonehenge private tours; but many platforms list non-Blue-Badge 'guides' who have no accreditation; (5) the bundled 'other sites' (Bath, Windsor, Avebury) are the actual margin generators — operators charge £350-£550 for 'Stonehenge + Bath' private tour but the actual extra cost over Stonehenge-only is £50-£80; (6) older travelers booking from North America with limited UK time are the target demographic — the appeal is 'door-to-door service' which is real but dramatically marked up; (7) legitimate licensed alternatives do exist: Premium Tours (with Inner Circle Access included at £199-£249 non-private + £80-£110 Stone Circle), Rabbie's Tours (Edinburgh-based, £95-£110 group coach), or Crown Coaches of Salisbury (private driver at £180-£280 per half-day). For older travelers wanting a Stonehenge tour: (1) for Inner Circle Access + transport, book separately — Inner Circle at english-heritage.org.uk (£80-£110) + train London-Salisbury (£25-£45) + Stonehenge Tour Bus (£17) = £122-£172 per person vs £279-£450 on a private tour; (2) if you want the private experience, verify the guide holds a Blue Badge Guide qualification — ask explicitly and check at britishguildoftouristguides.com; (3) for a genuine private car service, Crown Coaches (crowncoachessalisbury.com, Salisbury-based) offers private driver at £180-£280 per half-day — half the price of aggregator 'private tours'; (4) for a legitimate small-group experience, Rabbie's Tours (rabbies.com, 16-passenger max, genuine quality operators) at £95-£110 is excellent value; (5) refuse ALL 'private luxury' pitches above £250 per person — you're paying aggregator commission, not tour quality; (6) for 'Stonehenge + Bath' combos, direct train to Salisbury + Tour Bus to Stonehenge (morning) + train Salisbury-Bath via Bristol or direct (afternoon) is more flexible and costs £65-£105 total in transport; (7) if booking via Viator/GetYourGuide, confirm the SPECIFIC operator name (not just the listing) and verify Blue Badge Guide accreditation in writing before booking; (8) if overcharged or misled, dispute via UK Section 75 Consumer Credit Act (credit cards, min £100) or standard Visa/MC chargeback.
scams.avoidance: Book components separately — Inner Circle at english-heritage.org.uk (£80-110) + train (£25-45) + Tour Bus (£17) = £122-172 For private driver, Crown Coaches Salisbury (£180-280/half-day) — half the aggregator 'private tour' price For legitimate small-group, Rabbie's Tours (rabbies.com, 16-passenger) at £95-110 per person Verify Blue Badge Guide accreditation at britishguildoftouristguides.com before booking any 'private tour' Refuse ALL 'private luxury' pitches above £250 per person — aggregator commission-driven markup
scams.location: London Victoria, London Paddington pickups + Stonehenge Visitor Centre — targeting the 'private luxury Stonehenge tour' market
